key_highlights: ASX rallied into the weekend lifted by major banking stocks despite deepening domestic macro headwinds.
Australian housing market faces its worst downturn in 40 years as auction clearance rates drop to 2020 lows and home values are downgraded.
Government refusal to commit to net budget savings amplifies fiscal inflation pressure, complicating the RBA rate path.
Coles (COL.AX) suffers heavy market valuation hit as Woolworths (WOW.AX) takes market share in competitive grocery sector.
Energy market tightness escalates with rising jet fuel costs and potential domestic gas supply bottlenecks.

sectors.trend: Bank shares gained late in the week, yet face severe medium-term headwinds from the worst housing market slump since 2020.
sectors.implications: Mortgage growth will decelerate and loan impairment provisions may rise across major lenders (CBA.AX, WBC.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX).

sectors.trend: Intense grocery price competition and margin erosion leading to billions in market cap losses for Coles against Woolworths.
sectors.implications: Market share rotation favours WOW.AX over COL.AX; broader retail margins remain constrained by theft and operating costs.

sectors.trend: Severe downturn in residential valuations, plummeting auction volumes, and regulatory clampdowns on underquoting.
sectors.implications: Downside risks for residential developers (MGR.AX, SGP.AX); commercial and pub assets see selective high-valuation liquidity.

sectors.trend: Geopolitical refinery disruptions and impending domestic gas shortages drive up fuel and industrial power input costs.
sectors.implications: Positive pricing power for upstream gas and oil producers (WDS.AX, STO.AX); margin squeeze for transport and aviation (QAN.AX).

sectors.trend: Speculative micro-cap exploration activity in gold and lithium contrasts with macro caution surrounding global demand.
sectors.implications: Large-cap diversified miners (BHP.AX, RIO.AX) remain tied to Chinese demand; junior explorers offer volatile thematic trading.

key_themes: Housing market distress threatening mortgage book growth and consumer wealth effects
Fiscal policy inertia sustaining inflation and constraining RBA rate cut flexibility
Supermarket price wars driving divergence between ASX staples leaders
Energy supply constraints elevating transport and industrial operating costs

risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce exposure to leveraged residential REITs and high-beta mortgage-dependent lenders; favor diversified financials.

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Persistent Fiscal Inflation & Delayed RBA Easing
risk_assessment.mitigation: Hedge bond duration; overweight cash equivalents and companies with robust free-cash-flow yields and low leverage.

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Domestic and Global Energy Supply Shocks
risk_assessment.mitigation: Maintain tactical allocations in upstream energy producers (WDS.AX) to hedge against rising input and fuel costs.

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Fintech and Digital Asset Systemic Vulnerabilities
risk_assessment.mitigation: Focus fintech exposures on regulated wealth-management platforms (RZI.AX) while avoiding unhedged crypto-linked entities.

opportunities.recommendation: Long Woolworths vs Short Coles Long/Short Pair Trade
opportunities.rationale: Coles is ceding grocery market share and valuation, creating a relative outperformance window for Woolworths.

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight Upstream Oil and Gas Producers
opportunities.rationale: Refinery outages and anticipated domestic gas policy deficits support elevated realised pricing for Australian producers.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Underweight Residential Property Developers and High-Multiple Banks
defensive_moves.rationale: Sharp property price drops and auction market stagnation increase earnings vulnerability for property and retail banking.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hold AUD and Interest Rate Bond Hedges
defensive_moves.rationale: Fiscal expansion without net budget savings creates risk of sustained rate differentials and bond volatility.

market_outlook.short_term: ASX 200 (^AXJO) likely to consolidate in the 8,000–8,250 range; bank rebound capped by worsening housing metrics.
market_outlook.long_term: Subdued Australian equity growth over 6–12 months as property downturn and sticky inflation limit consumer discretionary demand.

Federal Government Mid-Year Economic and Fiscal Outlook (MYEFO)
